issue: Under 18 U.S.C. § 3582(c)(1)(A), must a prisoner fully exhaust BOP administrative appeals before filing a compassionate release motion, or may he file once 30 days pass after the warden receives the request, even if the warden denied it within that period?

sides.position: The prisoner must first let the BOP review the request and make a recommendation, or wait out 30 days in silence, before filing in court; a warden's denial within 30 days requires full administrative exhaustion.
cases: United States v. Gunn, 980 F.3d 1178 (10th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: The prisoner may file in federal court 30 days after the warden receives the request, regardless of any administrative appeals still available, so full exhaustion is not required.
cases: United States v. Alam, 960 F.3d 831 (6th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Harris, 973 F.3d 170 (3d Cir. 2020)

quote: The circuit courts also appear to be divided on this issue.
cite: United States v. Saladino, 7 F.4th 120 (2d Cir. 2021)
